title: Improved Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums
description: Improves the basic counting bound N ≥ (2^n-1)/n for Erdős Problem #1 by exploiting the distinctness of elements. Proves that n distinct naturals ≤ N have sum ≤ nN - n(n-1)/2, yielding the tighter bound N ≥ (2^n-1)/n + (n-1)/2. States the Dubroff-Fox-Xu bound.

meta.author: Original analysis, formalized in Lean 4
meta.assumptions: None. All results fully proved from Mathlib.
originalContributions: Generalized sum lower bound for distinct naturals ≥ c
Complement sum identity for bounded Finsets
Tight sum upper bound using distinctness: sum ≤ nN - n(n-1)/2

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #1 asks whether a set of n positive integers with all 2^n subset sums distinct must have maximum element ≥ c·2^n. The basic counting bound gives N ≥ (2^n-1)/n. Dubroff, Fox, and Xu (2021) proved the best known lower bound N ≥ Ω(2^n/√n). This formalization provides an intermediate improvement using the elementary observation that distinct integers bounded by N have constrained sums.
overview.problemStatement: Improve the lower bound on $N$ for sets $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ with $|A| = n$ and distinct subset sums. The basic counting bound gives $N \geq (2^n - 1)/n$. We prove $N \geq (2^n - 1)/n + (n-1)/2$.
overview.text: A formalization proving an improved lower bound for Erdős Problem #1 (distinct subset sums). The key insight is that n distinct elements bounded by N have sum at most nN - n(n-1)/2 (the complement argument), which combined with the DSS sum bound sum(A) ≥ 2^n - 1 yields a strictly better lower bound than counting alone.
overview.proofStrategy: Three-step proof: (1) Prove that n distinct naturals ≥ c have sum ≥ cn + n(n-1)/2, by induction extracting the minimum. (2) Apply the complement map a ↦ N-a to derive sum(A) ≤ nN - n(n-1)/2. (3) Combine with the DSS sum bound.
keyInsights: The complement map a ↦ N-a transforms the upper bound problem into a lower bound problem for distinct naturals
n distinct naturals have minimum sum n(n-1)/2 (the triangular number), proved by min-extraction induction
The improvement (n-1)/2 is small compared to 2^n/n but demonstrates the power of the distinctness constraint
The gap to the DFX bound (Ω(2^n/√n)) is a factor of √n in the leading term

sections.title: Sum Lower Bound for Distinct Naturals
sections.summary: Proves that n distinct naturals ≥ c have 2·sum ≥ n·(2c+n-1). Corollary: 2·sum ≥ n·(n-1) for c=0.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{i} b_i \geq cn + \binom{n}{2}$ for $n$ distinct naturals $b_i \geq c$

sections.title: Sum Upper Bound via Complement
sections.summary: Proves the complement sum identity and derives 2·sum(A) + n(n-1) ≤ 2nN for distinct elements ≤ N.
sections.mathContext: $2 \sum a_i + n(n-1) \leq 2nN$ for $n$ distinct naturals $a_i \leq N$

sections.title: Improved DSS Lower Bound
sections.summary: Combines DSS sum bound with distinctness upper bound to prove 2nN + 2 ≥ 2^(n+1) + n(n-1).
sections.mathContext: $2nN + 2 \geq 2^{n+1} + n(n-1)$ for DSS sets in $\{0, \ldots, N\}$

sections.title: Small Case Verification
sections.summary: Verifies the improved bound for n = 4, 5, 8.

sections.title: Dubroff-Fox-Xu Bound
sections.summary: States the DFX bound: N ≥ C · 2^n / √n for some C > 0.

crossReferences.description: Extends the Erdős #1 counting bound with a strictly stronger lower bound
OQ-03 studies the Conway-Guy upper bound; this studies improved lower bounds

conclusion.summary: An improved lower bound for Erdős Problem #1 is proved by combining the DSS sum bound with a tight upper bound on the sum of distinct bounded integers. The improvement is (n-1)/2 over the basic counting bound.
conclusion.implications: Demonstrates that elementary distinctness arguments can improve on the naive counting bound. The complement map technique may be useful for other extremal combinatorics formalizations.
openQuestions: Can the complement technique be refined further (e.g., using positivity to get sum ≤ nN - n²/2)?
Can the Dubroff-Fox-Xu probabilistic argument be formalized in Lean 4?
